notes:
ATTEMPT 3. The MAJOR is resolved and the option is finally legible.

The three attempts trace a clean diagnosis. Attempt 1 rendered a completely PLAIN back — which is the sibling option in this same field, so the image sold the wrong garment outright. Attempt 2 put two folds in the right places but rendered them as loose drape creases under flat frontal light, so a customer could not have told this from the plain-back sibling either. Attempt 3 changed the LIGHT, and that alone made the difference.

The principle is worth keeping, because it is the same one bias-outer-top-collar taught in a different form earlier today: SOME OPTIONS NEED A SPECIFIC PHOTOGRAPHIC CONDITION TO EXIST IN THE PICTURE AT ALL.

  - A grain direction is invisible on plain cloth   -> change the CLOTH (use a stripe)
  - A pressed fold is invisible under flat light    -> change the LIGHT (rake it hard across the surface)

In both cases the default condition is not neutral: it deletes the subject. A white pleat on white poplin has no colour and no pattern, so the shadow it casts is its only visual signal, and lighting stops being a stylistic choice.

All nine categories at or above 95 with zero Critical or Major findings, so this qualifies for the logged waiver at attempt 3.
